Hi! Welcome to TheUnexplained -- the subverse where we delve into the deepest mysteries and phenomena throughout history. I’m gr33narrow, and I’ll be assisting bill.lee in moderating. I’ve been lurking on this sub, occasionally chiming in, and talking to bill.lee on the IRC about various events. I cleared it with him, and I think now’s a good time to start a nice discussion!

What Makes a Good Unexplained Mystery?

This has been the source of my writing for some time. I remember when I was 10, I would hide out in the shelves of the library, reading things on UFOs. I would scour the web and read up on cases. I would stay up late and watch documentaries, much to the chagrin of my parents.

A lot of this will be nothing new to many of you, but to people not used to our X-Files style minds, I want to help out as much as possible!

But what makes something compelling? What makes something so alluring that people flock to it in hopes of uncovering “The Truth?” Let’s explore that, shall we?

The Case

As all good mysteries go, we begin with a story. These cases, whether it’s a first hand account or a newspaper clipping are what get the ball rolling. From a guy talking about a UFO to archaeological findings, there is always more to the story.

-When investigating the story, it’s always good to look at the credibility of the source. While not a fool-proof indicator of truth (sometimes the “crazy” people may have more truth than the “sane” ones), it’s always valuable. If your source has a history of lying, but it’s a compelling story, see if there are other sources to substantiate the claims. If so....

-Do the sources have similar claims? What about their stories line up? What about their findings line up? What differs? Where is the source material coming from. Remember: it is always important to have at least one credible source, whether it’s a newspaper article, government doc, journal, or other media.

-Look for keywords in your case. Location is always a big one. If this source is talking about a UFO, but lives next to a military base, then there’s a high potential for experimental aircraft --- a story in and of itself. However: that doesn’t mean the mystery ends there. In fact, a whole new can of worms can be opened.

The Research

-Looking up the history of a location, as previously mentioned, is recommended. Nothing more to add.

-Presenting a case is one thing. Doing further research on it makes it so much more compelling. Example: I start researching a case on a UFO sighting in Missouri. I check to see if there is a military base nearby. There is. This military base is home to a few experimental test flights in the early 90s. However, the plot thickens when I find that a similar case was found in Europe. That’s when my research can really take off. -If at all possible, having government documents (censored or not) can add to any case. Police files are an often overlooked part as well. If something strange happens, people will call their local police station and report it. A newer growing medium for sources are blogs. While less credible, it can add to your case when used in conjunction with other research (E.G. Who really killed Mr. Body? The official report says one thing, but....blogs point you in another direction and you find the police work,.. well, sloppy.)

-Look for anomalies in files. Sometimes things don’t add up. (E.G. They convicted someone, but the DNA didn’t match. They got the person on weak circumstantial evidence. It’s our goal to explore it.)

The Presentation of your Case

-I always recommend starting by presenting your case in a sort of “thesis” format. First the What, then the Why, and then substantiate it.

-Welcome any and all criticism. If you are met with a challenge and you can overcome it, that makes your case stronger.

-Leave it open to more ideas. Working as a group gets more accomplished than working alone. Think of it as a peer review.

That’s all Folks!

If you have anything to add, go for it in the comment section! I am really happy to be here and I love reading all the fun new cases. I do my own research on some of it and let me tell you, many hours were spent sifting through these topics!
